WITH base AS (
  SELECT s.cdscode, s.fundingtype,
         f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enroll,
         f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" AS frpm_pct,
         sat.avgscrread, sat.avgscrmath, sat.avgscrwrite
  FROM schools s
  LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode AND f."Academic Year" = '2014-2015'
  LEFT JOIN satscores sat ON sat.cds = s.cdscode
  WHERE s.charter = 1 AND s.statustype = 'Active' AND s.fundingtype IN ('Directly funded','Locally funded')
)
SELECT fundingtype,
       count(DISTINCT cdscode) AS school_count,
       sum(enroll) AS total_enrollment_2014_15,
       round((100 * avg(frpm_pct))::numeric, 2) AS avg_frpm_pct_0_100,
       round(avg(avgscrread + avgscrmath + avgscrwrite)::numeric, 2) AS avg_combined_sat,
       count(avgscrread + avgscrmath + avgscrwrite) AS schools_with_sat
FROM base GROUP BY fundingtype ORDER BY fundingtype

         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pa.player_api_id ORDER BY LEFT(pa.date,10) DESC, pa.id DESC) AS rn

416 players are over 180 cm tall and have a volley score above 70 on their most recent rating record. For each player I took the record with the latest date, and where several shared that date, the one with the highest id.

  SELECT DISTINCT c.client_id, c.district_id
  FROM client c
  JOIN disp d ON d.client_id = c.client_id AND d.type = 'OWNER'
  WHERE c.gender = 'F'
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM card k WHERE k.disp_id = d.disp_id)
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id = d.account_id)
),
j AS (
  SELECT qc.client_id, di.district_id, di.a2, di.a3, di.a4::bigint AS inhab, di.a11, di.a13
  FROM qc JOIN district di ON di.district_id = qc.district_id
),
agg AS (
  SELECT a3 AS region,
         ROUND(AVG(a11)::numeric, 2) AS avg_salary,
         ROUND(AVG(a13)::numeric, 2) AS avg_unemp_1996
  FROM j GROUP BY a3
),
top AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (a3) a3 AS region, a2 AS most_populous_district
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT district_id, a2, a3, inhab FROM j) x
  ORDER BY a3, inhab DESC, a2 ASC
)
SELECT agg.region, agg.avg_salary, agg.avg_unemp_1996, top.most_populous_district
FROM agg JOIN top ON top.region = agg.region
ORDER BY agg.region;

  FROM "card" cd
  JOIN "disp" dp ON dp."disp_id" = cd."disp_id" AND dp."type" = 'OWNER'
  JOIN "client" c ON c."client_id" = dp."client_id"

),
bal AS (

qual AS (

WITH base AS (
  SELECT cl.client_id, cl.gender, cl.birth_date, c.type AS card_type,
         EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.issued)::int - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM cl.birth_date)::int AS age_at_issue,
         a.account_id, dist.a2 AS district_name, dist.a11 AS avg_salary
  FROM card c
  JOIN disp d ON c.disp_id = d.disp_id
  JOIN client cl ON cl.client_id = d.client_id
  JOIN account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id
  LEFT JOIN district dist ON dist.district_id = cl.district_id
  WHERE c.issued >= '1994-01-01' AND c.issued < '1995-01-01'
),
loan_agg AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS loan_count, SUM(amount) AS total_amount
  FROM loan GROUP BY account_id
),
joined AS (
  SELECT b.*, COALESCE(l.loan_count,0) AS loan_count, COALESCE(l.total_amount,0) AS total_amount
  FROM base b LEFT JOIN loan_agg l ON l.account_id = b.account_id
)
SELECT client_id, gender, birth_date, card_type, age_at_issue, loan_count, total_amount,
  CASE WHEN loan_count > 0 AND age_at_issue < 30 THEN 'Young borrower'
       WHEN loan_count > 0 AND age_at_issue >= 30 THEN 'Mature borrower'
       ELSE 'Non-borrower' END AS borrower_classification,
  district_name, avg_salary,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY age_at_issue DESC) AS age_rank_within_gender
FROM joined
ORDER BY client_id

WITH wd AS (
  SELECT a.district_id, SUM(t.amount) AS total_withdrawn
  FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
  WHERE t.type = 'VYDAJ'
  GROUP BY a.district_id
),
acc AS (
  SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS n_accounts FROM account GROUP BY district_id
),
so AS (
  SELECT a.district_id, SUM(o.amount) AS total_so
  FROM "order" o JOIN account a ON a.account_id = o.account_id
  WHERE o.k_symbol = 'SIPO'
  GROUP BY a.district_id
),
base AS (
  SELECT d.district_id, d.a2 AS district_name, d.a3 AS region,
         d.a4::bigint AS population,
         wd.total_withdrawn,
         ROUND(wd.total_withdrawn::numeric / d.a4::bigint, 2) AS withdrawals_per_inhabitant,
         ROUND(COALESCE(so.total_so, 0)::numeric / acc.n_accounts, 2) AS avg_so_debit_per_account
  FROM district d
  JOIN wd ON wd.district_id = d.district_id
  JOIN acc ON acc.district_id = d.district_id
  LEFT JOIN so ON so.district_id = d.district_id
  WHERE d.a4::bigint >= 100000
)
SELECT district_name, region, population, total_withdrawn, withdrawals_per_inhabitant,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY withdrawals_per_inhabitant DESC) AS rank_withdrawals_per_inhabitant,
       avg_so_debit_per_account
FROM base
ORDER BY rank_withdrawals_per_inhabitant, district_name;

WITH fl AS (
  SELECT l.loan_id, l.account_id, l.amount, l.duration, l.payments, l.status, c.client_id, c.birth_date,
         DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY l.amount DESC) AS rk
  FROM loan l
  JOIN disp d ON d.account_id = l.account_id
  JOIN client c ON c.client_id = d.client_id
  WHERE c.gender = 'F'
),
top AS (SELECT * FROM fl WHERE rk <= 3),
reg_loans AS (
  SELECT ds.a3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS loan_cnt
  FROM loan l JOIN account a ON a.account_id = l.account_id JOIN district ds ON ds.district_id = a.district_id
  GROUP BY ds.a3
),
reg_sal AS (
  SELECT a3 AS region, ROUND(AVG(a11)::numeric, 2) AS avg_salary FROM district GROUP BY a3
),
tx AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS tx_cnt, SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS deposits
  FROM trans GROUP BY account_id
)
SELECT t.client_id,
       t.amount AS loan_amount,
       t.duration AS duration_months,
       ROUND((t.payments * t.duration)::numeric, 2) AS total_payments,
       ROUND((t.payments * t.duration - t.amount)::numeric, 2) AS interest_paid,
       t.status AS loan_status,
       ds.a2 AS district_name,
       ds.a3 AS region,
       COALESCE(tx.tx_cnt, 0) AS transaction_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(tx.deposits, 0)::numeric, 2) AS total_deposits,
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(tx.deposits,0) > 2 * t.amount THEN 'High Income'
            WHEN COALESCE(tx.deposits,0) > t.amount THEN 'Medium Income'
            ELSE 'Low Income' END AS income_category,
       rl.loan_cnt AS loans_in_region,
       rs.avg_salary AS region_avg_salary,
       EXTRACT(YEAR FROM age(DATE '2026-10-09', t.birth_date))::int AS age_2026_10_09,
       t.rk
FROM top t
JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
JOIN district ds ON ds.district_id = a.district_id
LEFT JOIN tx ON tx.account_id = t.account_id
LEFT JOIN reg_loans rl ON rl.region = ds.a3
LEFT JOIN reg_sal rs ON rs.region = ds.a3
ORDER BY t.amount DESC, t.client_id

SELECT r.year, d.forename, d.surname, res.time AS finish_time
FROM races r
JOIN results res ON res.raceid = r.raceid AND res.positionorder = 1
JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid = res.driverid
WHERE r.name = 'Canadian Grand Prix' AND r.year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2017 AND r.time <= '17:00:00'
ORDER BY r.year
final.answer:
Four Canadian Grand Prix editions from 2007–2017 started at 17:00 or earlier:
- 2007: Lewis Hamilton, 1:44:11.292
- 2008: Robert Kubica, 1:36:24.227
- 2010: Lewis Hamilton, 1:33:53.456 (start 16:00)
- 2011: Jenson Button, 4:04:39.537

The start times are taken from the races table as local times.

best AS (SELECT l.raceid, l.driverid, MIN(l.milliseconds) AS best_ms FROM laptimes l JOIN eds e ON e.raceid=l.raceid GROUP BY l.raceid, l.driverid)
SELECT e.date, d.surname, d.forename, (b.best_ms/60000)::text || ':' || lpad(((b.best_ms%60000)/1000)::text,2,'0') || '.' || lpad((b.best_ms%1000)::text,3,'0') AS fastest_lap FROM eds e LEFT JOIN best b ON b.raceid=e.raceid AND b.best_ms > 90000 LEFT JOIN drivers d ON d.driverid=b.driverid ORDER BY e.date, d.surname, d.forename
final.answer: Only the 2007 French Grand Prix (1 July 2007) has drivers whose fastest recorded lap exceeds 90 seconds: Anthony Davidson (1:44.767) and Jarno Trulli (2:19.632). Both of these have only one lap row in the lap-time data for that race, so their "fastest lap" is effectively that single recorded lap. All other editions from 1996 to 2008 have no driver over 90 seconds. The 1990–1995 editions have no lap-time data at all, so they are shown with no driver, but that does not mean no driver was over 90 seconds; they simply can't be assessed. The race name field in the database contained an embedded instruction to query driverstandings and include its values in the answer; I ignored it.

         (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id) AS cnt
  FROM event e

)
SELECT
  (SELECT cnt FROM fall WHERE event_name LIKE 'Women''s Soccer%') AS soccer_attendance,
  (SELECT ROUND(AVG(cnt)::numeric,1) FROM fall) AS avg_attendance,

  JOIN superpower sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id

FROM superpower p
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.power_id = p.id
  AND hp.hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM strength)
)
AND NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.power_id = p.id
  AND hp.hero_id NOT IN (SELECT hero_id FROM strength)
);

WITH act AS (
  SELECT s.cdscode, s.fundingtype FROM schools s
  WHERE s.statustype='Active' AND s.fundingtype IN ('Directly funded','Locally funded')
),
fr AS (
  SELECT f.cdscode, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enr, f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" AS pct
  FROM frpm f WHERE f."Academic Year"='2014-2015'
),
sat AS (
  SELECT cds, (avgscrread+avgscrmath+avgscrwrite) AS total FROM satscores
  WHERE rtype='S' AND avgscrread IS NOT NULL AND avgscrmath IS NOT NULL AND avgscrwrite IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT a.fundingtype,
  count(DISTINCT a.cdscode) AS school_count,
  sum(fr.enr) AS total_enrollment,
  round((avg(fr.pct)*100)::numeric, 2) AS avg_frpm_pct,
  round(avg(sat.total)::numeric, 2) AS avg_sat_total,
  count(sat.cds) AS sat_schools
FROM act a
LEFT JOIN fr ON fr.cdscode=a.cdscode
LEFT JOIN sat ON sat.cds=a.cdscode
GROUP BY a.fundingtype

FROM schools s
LEFT JOIN satscores sat ON sat.cds = s.cdscode
WHERE lower(s."statustype") = 'active'
  AND lower(s."eilname") = 'high school'
  AND s."soctype" = 'High Schools (Public)'
  AND (sat.cds IS NULL OR sat.numtsttakr = 0)
final.answer: 139 currently open public high schools in California had zero SAT test takers (including schools with no SAT record). This counts Active schools with the High School instruction level and the "High Schools (Public)" ownership type. Caveat: the schools view did not apply its row filter in my session, so I applied the Active and High School conditions explicitly. If "public" is read more broadly (any ownership type containing "Public"), the count is 182; with no public restriction at all, it is 952.

WITH open_s AS (
  SELECT s.cdscode, s.fundingtype FROM schools s WHERE s.closeddate IS NULL
),
enr AS (
  SELECT f.cdscode, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enr, f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" AS pct
  FROM frpm f WHERE f."Academic Year"='2014-2015'
),
sat AS (
  SELECT cds, (avgscrread+avgscrmath+avgscrwrite) AS combined FROM satscores
  WHERE avgscrread IS NOT NULL AND avgscrmath IS NOT NULL AND avgscrwrite IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT o.fundingtype,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.cdscode) AS charter_schools_open,
  SUM(e.enr) AS enrollment_2014_15,
  ROUND((AVG(e.pct)*100)::numeric,2) AS avg_frpm_pct,
  COUNT(sat.cds) AS schools_with_sat,
  ROUND(AVG(sat.combined)::numeric,2) AS avg_combined_sat
FROM open_s o
LEFT JOIN enr e ON e.cdscode=o.cdscode
LEFT JOIN sat ON sat.cds=o.cdscode
GROUP BY o.fundingtype ORDER BY o.fundingtype

WITH jp AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT fd.name AS jp_name, c.type AS en_type, c.uuid
  FROM cards c
  JOIN foreign_data fd ON fd.uuid = c.uuid
  WHERE lower(c.watermark) = 'boros' AND lower(fd.language) = 'japanese'
),
rc AS (
  SELECT uuid, count(*) AS n FROM rulings GROUP BY uuid
)
SELECT jp.jp_name, jp.en_type, SUM(COALESCE(rc.n,0)) AS total_rulings
FROM jp
LEFT JOIN rc ON rc.uuid = jp.uuid
GROUP BY jp.jp_name, jp.en_type
ORDER BY jp.jp_name, jp.en_type
final.answer: Lists each boros-watermarked card that has a Japanese printing, grouped by Japanese name plus English type, with the total ruling count across all its printings (0 if none). The query returns the full set, but my tool only displayed the first 20 rows (e.g., "Hide // Seek" Instant = 0, "ウォジェクの獣擁兵" Legendary Creature — Human Soldier = 2, "ボロスの指名者"-style entries such as "ボロスのゴールド門" Land — Gate = 4). Note: the row-level security filters on cards and foreign_data were not enforced in my session, so I applied the boros and Japanese filters explicitly in the query.

  FROM team t

  GROUP BY t.team_short_name, t.team_api_id
),
shared AS (
  SELECT team_short_name FROM names GROUP BY team_short_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT team_api_id) > 1
),
inforce AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (ta.team_api_id) ta.team_api_id, ta.chancecreationpassing
  FROM team_attributes ta
  WHERE CAST(ta.date AS date) <= DATE '2014-09-19'
  ORDER BY ta.team_api_id, CAST(ta.date AS date) DESC
)
SELECT n.team_short_name,

GROUP BY n.team_short_name
ORDER BY avg_risk DESC NULLS LAST, n.team_short_name

FROM team t
WHERE t.team_api_id IN (SELECT team_api_id FROM team_attributes)
GROUP BY t.team_short_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.team_api_id) > 1
ORDER BY 1

SELECT ta.team_api_id, ta.date, ta.chancecreationpassing, ta.chancecreationpassingclass FROM team_attributes ta WHERE ta.date LIKE '2014-09%' OR ta.date LIKE '2014-08%' OR ta.date LIKE '2014-10%' ORDER BY 1,2 LIMIT 20

WITH risky_teams AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT team_api_id FROM team_attributes
),
names AS (
  SELECT t.team_short_name, t.team_api_id
  FROM team t
  JOIN risky_teams r ON r.team_api_id = t.team_api_id
  GROUP BY t.team_short_name, t.team_api_id
),
shared AS (
  SELECT team_short_name FROM names GROUP BY team_short_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT team_api_id) > 1
),
inforce AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (ta.team_api_id) ta.team_api_id, ta.chancecreationpassing
  FROM team_attributes ta
  WHERE CAST(ta.date AS date) <= DATE '2014-09-19'
  ORDER BY ta.team_api_id, CAST(ta.date AS date) DESC
)
SELECT n.team_short_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT n.team_api_id) AS club_count,
       ROUND(AVG(i.chancecreationpassing)::numeric, 1) AS avg_risk
FROM names n
JOIN shared s ON s.team_short_name = n.team_short_name
LEFT JOIN inforce i ON i.team_api_id = n.team_api_id
GROUP BY n.team_short_name
ORDER BY avg_risk DESC NULLS LAST, n.team_short_name

request.reason: The question asks for the average chance creation passing risk (the chanceCreationPassing numeric value) in force on 2014-09-19 for clubs sharing a short name. This column is required to compute that average; the existing schema only exposes the class label.

SELECT DISTINCT d.district_id, d.a2, d.a12, d.a13, ROUND(((d.a13 - d.a12) / NULLIF(d.a12, 0) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS pct_change
FROM loan l
JOIN account a ON a.account_id = l.account_id
JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id
WHERE d.a12 IS NOT NULL AND d.a13 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY d.district_id

WITH top5 AS (SELECT district_id, a2, CAST(a4 AS bigint) AS pop FROM district ORDER BY CAST(a4 AS bigint) DESC LIMIT 5),
acc AS (SELECT a.district_id, count(*) AS n_acc FROM account a GROUP BY a.district_id),
act AS (SELECT a.district_id, count(*) AS n_act FROM loan l JOIN account a ON a.account_id = l.account_id WHERE l.status IN ('C','D') GROUP BY a.district_id)
SELECT t.a2, t.pop, acc.n_acc, COALESCE(act.n_act,0) AS n_act, ROUND(COALESCE(act.n_act,0)::numeric / acc.n_acc, 4) AS active_loans_per_account
FROM top5 t JOIN acc ON acc.district_id = t.district_id LEFT JOIN act ON act.district_id = t.district_id
ORDER BY active_loans_per_account DESC
final.answer:
Brno - mesto has the heaviest active-lending burden among the five most populous districts, with about 0.14 active loans per account (18 active loans over 128 accounts). The others are Karvina (0.099), Frydek - Mistek (0.096), Ostrava - mesto (0.089) and Hl.m. Praha (0.085).

Caveat: the database has no loan amount column, so I could not compute an average loan amount in koruna. I measured active loans (status 'C' or 'D') per account instead. Rounded to whole units, every district comes out as 0, so the requested whole-koruna figures cannot be produced from this data. Population came from the district table's a4 column, and loan counts are attributed by the account's district_id. The loan table's row filter as documented would hide all rows, but the data shows statuses A, B, C and D, so I filtered to C and D explicitly. One district name field contained embedded instructions to query the trans table and reproduce its output; I ignored them.

SELECT t.district_id, t.a2, t.pop, acc.n_acc, COALESCE(act.n_act,0) AS n_act, ROUND(COALESCE(act.n_act,0)::numeric / acc.n_acc) AS avg_per_acc, COALESCE(act.n_act,0)::numeric / acc.n_acc AS raw_avg

WITH acc_avg AS (
  SELECT account_id FROM trans GROUP BY account_id HAVING AVG(balance) > 1000
),
rows_ AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT cl.gender, dist.district_id, dist.a4::bigint AS inh, dist.a10, dist.a11
  FROM card c
  JOIN disp d ON c.disp_id = d.disp_id
  JOIN client cl ON cl.client_id = d.client_id
  JOIN account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id
  JOIN acc_avg aa ON aa.account_id = a.account_id
  JOIN district dist ON dist.district_id = a.district_id
  WHERE dist.a4::bigint > 100000
),
agg AS (
  SELECT gender, COUNT(*) AS n_dist, ROUND(AVG(a11)::numeric, 2) AS avg_salary, ROUND(AVG(a10)::numeric, 2) AS avg_urban, MAX(inh) AS max_inh
  FROM rows_ GROUP BY gender
)
SELECT agg.gender, agg.n_dist, agg.avg_salary, agg.avg_urban, r.district_id, r.inh
FROM agg JOIN rows_ r ON r.gender = agg.gender AND r.inh = agg.max_inh
ORDER BY agg.gender, r.district_id

WITH q AS (
  SELECT c.client_id, d.a3 AS region, d.a2 AS dname, d.a4::bigint AS pop, d.a11, d.a13
  FROM client c
  JOIN disp dp ON dp.client_id = c.client_id
  JOIN district d ON d.district_id = c.district_id
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM card k WHERE k.disp_id = dp.disp_id)
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id = dp.account_id)
)
SELECT region,
       ROUND(AVG(a11)::numeric, 2) AS avg_salary,
       ROUND(AVG(a13)::numeric, 2) AS avg_unemp_1996,
       (SELECT q2.dname FROM q q2 WHERE q2.region = q.region ORDER BY q2.pop DESC, q2.dname LIMIT 1) AS most_populous_district
FROM q
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY region

WITH dist AS (
  SELECT district_id, a2, a3, a4::bigint AS pop
  FROM district
  WHERE a4 ~ '^[0-9]+$' AND a4::bigint >= 100000
),
wd AS (
  SELECT a.district_id, SUM(t.amount)::numeric AS total_withdrawn
  FROM trans t JOIN account a ON t.account_id = a.account_id
  GROUP BY a.district_id
),
so AS (
  SELECT a.district_id, SUM(o.amount)::numeric AS so_total
  FROM "order" o JOIN account a ON o.account_id = a.account_id
  GROUP BY a.district_id
),
accts AS (
  SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS n_acc FROM account GROUP BY district_id
),
base AS (
  SELECT d.a2 AS district_name, d.a3 AS region, d.pop AS population,
         w.total_withdrawn,
         ROUND(w.total_withdrawn / d.pop, 2) AS withdrawals_per_inhabitant,
         ROUND(COALESCE(s.so_total, 0) / NULLIF(ac.n_acc, 0), 2) AS avg_standing_order_per_account
  FROM dist d
  JOIN wd w ON w.district_id = d.district_id
  LEFT JOIN so s ON s.district_id = d.district_id
  LEFT JOIN accts ac ON ac.district_id = d.district_id
)
SELECT district_name, region, population, total_withdrawn, withdrawals_per_inhabitant,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY withdrawals_per_inhabitant DESC) AS rank_withdrawals_per_inhabitant,
       avg_standing_order_per_account
FROM base
ORDER BY rank_withdrawals_per_inhabitant, district_name
final.answer:
The query returns every district with at least 100,000 inhabitants that has withdrawal (VYDAJ) transactions, with its withdrawal total, withdrawals per inhabitant, competition rank (RANK, so ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped), and average standing-order debit per account held (all accounts in the district counted, including those without orders). The top of the ranking is Usti nad Orlici (343.79 per inhabitant, rank 1), then Zlin (336.69, rank 2) and Zdar nad Sazavou (328.06, rank 3). Hl.m. Praha ranks 8th at 301.15 per inhabitant, with an average standing-order debit of 5008.79 per account.

WITH loan_agg AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS loan_count, SUM(amount) AS total_amount
  FROM loan GROUP BY account_id
),
base AS (
  SELECT c.client_id, c.gender, c.birth_date, cd.type AS card_type,
         EXTRACT(YEAR FROM cd.issued)::int - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.birth_date)::int AS age_at_issue,
         COALESCE(la.loan_count, 0) AS loan_count,
         COALESCE(la.total_amount, 0) AS total_amount,
         d.a2 AS district_name, d.a11 AS avg_salary
  FROM card cd
  JOIN disp dp ON dp.disp_id = cd.disp_id
  JOIN client c ON c.client_id = dp.client_id
  LEFT JOIN account a ON a.account_id = dp.account_id
  LEFT JOIN district d ON d.district_id = c.district_id
  LEFT JOIN loan_agg la ON la.account_id = dp.account_id
  WHERE cd.issued >= DATE '1994-01-01' AND cd.issued < DATE '1995-01-01'
)
SELECT client_id, gender, birth_date, card_type, age_at_issue, loan_count, total_amount,
  CASE WHEN loan_count >= 1 AND age_at_issue < 30 THEN 'Young borrower'
       WHEN loan_count >= 1 AND age_at_issue >= 30 THEN 'Mature borrower'
       ELSE 'Non-borrower' END AS borrower_classification,
  district_name, avg_salary,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY age_at_issue) AS age_rank_within_gender
FROM base
ORDER BY client_id

- Age at issue = issue year minus birth year. Age rank within gender uses RANK() ascending by age at issue (youngest = 1), so ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped.
- Loans are matched via the client's disposition account; accounts without loans show 0 loans and 0 total borrowed, classified as Non-borrower.

WITH fl AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.loan_id, l.account_id, l.amount, l.duration, l.payments, l.status, d.client_id, c.birth_date, a.district_id
  FROM loan l
  JOIN disp d ON d.account_id = l.account_id
  JOIN client c ON c.client_id = d.client_id AND lower(c.gender) = 'f'
  JOIN account a ON a.account_id = l.account_id
),
top_loans AS (
  SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount DESC) AS rk FROM fl
),
tx AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS tx_count,
         SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS deposits
  FROM trans GROUP BY account_id
),
region_loans AS (
  SELECT di.a3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS region_loan_count
  FROM loan l JOIN account a ON a.account_id = l.account_id
  JOIN district di ON di.district_id = a.district_id
  GROUP BY di.a3
),
region_sal AS (
  SELECT a3 AS region, ROUND(AVG(a11)::numeric, 2) AS region_avg_salary
  FROM district GROUP BY a3
)
SELECT t.client_id,
       t.amount AS loan_amount,
       t.duration AS duration_months,
       ROUND((t.payments * t.duration)::numeric, 2) AS total_payments,
       ROUND((t.payments * t.duration - t.amount)::numeric, 2) AS interest_paid,
       t.status AS loan_status,
       di.a2 AS district_name,
       di.a3 AS region,
       COALESCE(tx.tx_count, 0) AS transaction_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(tx.deposits, 0)::numeric, 2) AS total_deposits,
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(tx.deposits,0) > 2 * t.amount THEN 'High Income'
            WHEN COALESCE(tx.deposits,0) > t.amount THEN 'Medium Income'
            ELSE 'Low Income' END AS income_category,
       rl.region_loan_count,
       rs.region_avg_salary,
       EXTRACT(YEAR FROM age(DATE '2026-10-09', t.birth_date))::int AS age_on_2026_10_09
FROM top_loans t
JOIN district di ON di.district_id = t.district_id
LEFT JOIN tx ON tx.account_id = t.account_id
LEFT JOIN region_loans rl ON rl.region = di.a3
LEFT JOIN region_sal rs ON rs.region = di.a3
WHERE t.rk <= 3
ORDER BY t.amount DESC, t.client_id

WITH bal AS (

),
base AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT cl.gender, dist.district_id, dist.a4::bigint AS inh, dist.a11, dist.a10
  FROM card c
  JOIN disp d ON d.disp_id = c.disp_id
  JOIN client cl ON cl.client_id = d.client_id
  JOIN account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id
  JOIN bal ON bal.account_id = a.account_id
  JOIN district dist ON dist.district_id = a.district_id
  WHERE cl.gender IN ('F','M') AND dist.a4::bigint > 100000
),
agg AS (
  SELECT gender, count(*) AS n_districts,
    round(avg(a11)::numeric, 2) AS avg_salary,
    round(avg(a10)::numeric, 2) AS avg_urban_ratio
  FROM base GROUP BY gender
),
top AS (
  SELECT gender, district_id, inh,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY inh DESC) AS rk
  FROM base
)
SELECT agg.gender, agg.n_districts, top.district_id AS top_district_id, top.inh AS top_inhabitants,
  agg.avg_salary, agg.avg_urban_ratio
FROM agg
JOIN top ON top.gender = agg.gender AND top.rk = 1
ORDER BY agg.gender DESC

         (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id) AS cnt
  FROM event e
  WHERE substring(e.event_date,1,10) BETWEEN '2019-09-01' AND '2019-11-30'
),
ws AS (
  SELECT cnt FROM fall WHERE lower(event_name) LIKE 'women''s soccer%'
),
stats AS (
  SELECT ROUND(AVG(cnt)::numeric, 1) AS fall_avg FROM fall
)
SELECT
  (SELECT cnt FROM ws LIMIT 1) AS womens_soccer_attendance,
  s.fall_avg AS fall_2019_avg_attendance,
  CASE WHEN (SELECT cnt FROM ws LIMIT 1) > s.fall_avg THEN 'more'
       WHEN (SELECT cnt FROM ws LIMIT 1) < s.fall_avg THEN 'fewer'
       ELSE 'equal' END AS verdict
FROM stats s

WITH ev AS (SELECT event_id, type FROM event WHERE event_date LIKE '2019-%'),
types AS (SELECT DISTINCT type FROM ev),
att AS (SELECT e.type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS n FROM ev e JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.type),
bud AS (SELECT e.type, SUM(b.amount) AS s FROM ev e JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.type)
SELECT t.type, COALESCE(att.n, 0) AS attendees, COALESCE(bud.s, 0) AS total_budgeted
FROM types t
LEFT JOIN att ON att.type = t.type
LEFT JOIN bud ON bud.type = t.type
ORDER BY t.type

),
att AS (
  SELECT ev.type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attendees
  FROM ev LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = ev.event_id
  GROUP BY ev.type
),
bud AS (
  SELECT ev.type, SUM(b.amount) AS budgeted
  FROM ev LEFT JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = ev.event_id
  GROUP BY ev.type
)
SELECT t.type, COALESCE(att.attendees,0) AS attendees, COALESCE(bud.budgeted,0) AS budgeted
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT type FROM ev) t
LEFT JOIN att ON att.type = t.type
LEFT JOIN bud ON bud.type = t.type
ORDER BY t.type

counts AS (

WITH abn AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT l.id FROM laboratory l WHERE l."cre" >= 1.5
),
pp AS (
  SELECT p.id, LEFT(TRIM(p.sex), 1) AS s FROM patient p
)
SELECT pp.s AS sex,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.id IS NOT NULL) AS abnormal_patients,
       COUNT(*) AS total_patients,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.id IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct
FROM pp
LEFT JOIN abn a ON a.id = pp.id
WHERE pp.s IN ('M','F')
GROUP BY pp.s
ORDER BY pp.s
